title: Berlin U-Bahn Lines - FAQ
subtitle: Narrow trains, wide trains, the boards on the U5 and the new trains.

items.q: Which Berlin U-Bahn lines have the narrow trains?
items.a: The **U1, U2, U3 and U4** run on the narrow **Kleinprofil** network. Their cars are about **2.30 m** wide on the classic design and about **2.40 m** on newer trains.

items.q: Which lines have the wide trains?
items.a: The **U5, U6, U7, U8 and U9** run on the wide **Grossprofil** network, with cars about **2.65 m** wide and about **3.4 m** high.

items.q: Why does Berlin have two widths of U-Bahn train?
items.a: The first line opened in **1902** with cars close to tram width, and the lines built until **1913** kept that size. The Nord-Süd-Bahn, today's **U6**, opened wide on **30 January 1923**, and every line after it followed.

items.q: Can a U2 train run on the U7?
items.a: Not in service. Besides the width, the two networks take power differently: narrow trains press their shoe **on top** of the third rail, wide trains **from below**, with reversed polarity. Two track links exist only for moving trains.

items.q: What are the boards under the doors on the U5?
items.a: Some U5 trains are **IK** cars, a narrow-network design with a raised body. Since **October 2017** they carry boards along the lower body that bridge about **17.5 cm** to the wide platforms. Berliners call them **Blumenbretter**.

items.q: Where do the new J and JK trains run?
items.a: The narrow **JK** carried its first passengers on the **U2** on **8 September 2025**. The wide **J** entered regular service on the **U5** on **18 May 2026** and has run on the **U9** since early **October 2026**.

items.q: Which U-Bahn line is the busiest?
items.a: The **U7**, with about **463,100** riders on an average weekday in 2024 according to the Berlin Senate, ahead of the **U8** and the **U6**. All three are wide lines.
